summary: Spies, Lies & Supplies is a standalone 18-card expansion for Air, Land & Sea, swapping in Intelligence, Diplomacy, and Economics theaters for a fast, tight two-player bluffing duel over three simultaneous mini-battles. Reviewers say it keeps the same elegant push-and-pull tension as the original but shifts the flavor toward information warfare and hidden-info plays rather than raw power swings.
praised: High variety from just 18 new cards, with abilities that add flavor without new rules overhead
Espionage/information theme gives real counterplay — reading and predicting opponent's hand
Mixes cleanly with the base game or other expansions for more theater combinations
criticised: New cards feel less punchy/decisive than the original Air, Land & Sea deck
Many cards carry sacrificial costs, which some found less satisfying than direct aggression
Adds little necessity for owners who already have the base game; the 5-theater 'Epic Mode' didn't land for one reviewer

interaction.kind: direct card-vs-card confrontation across shared theaters
interaction.detail: Each theater (here Intelligence, Diplomacy, Economics) is a shared battlefield where a card's value depends entirely on what the opponent commits there, and abilities routinely flip, remove, or copy the opponent's cards. There is no private board at all — the three theaters are the entire game state, contested every turn.
interaction.said: unknown — no strong recalled reputation for this specific expansion module, falling back on the base Air, Land & Sea system, which players describe as a tight two-player duel where "every card is a threat or a bluff aimed straight at your opponent"

sources: card strength values contributed to each theater
theater point value awarded to the majority holder when a theater resolves
scoring.how_you_win: Play cards each round to hold the majority in at least two of the three theaters, banking each theater's point value; first player to reach 12 total points (or one who controls every theater at once, an instant win) takes the game.
scoring.score_note: first to 12+ pts at round end wins
